summary: Switzerland's Federal Statistical Office publishes child victims and accused of sexual acts with children by nationality and residence status every year, plus child assault victimization rates by nationality group and homicide and trafficking figures by residence status. All of this is nationality, a proxy, never ethnicity.

harms.label: Sexual acts with children (Art. 187, police)
harms.intro: Police recorded 1,118 offences of sexual acts with children (art. 187 of the Criminal Code) in 2025, with 986 victims (421 under 10, 387 aged 10-14, 157 aged 15-17) and 784 accused. The Federal Statistical Office publishes both victims and accused by nationality and residence status every year.

'Swiss' includes naturalised citizens; 'permanent foreign residents' hold B or C permits; 'asylum population' holds F, N or S permits; 'other foreigners' are short-term residents, cross-border workers, tourists, people without legal status or with status unknown.

breakdown.why: The Federal Statistical Office's police statistics give the 986 victims of sexual acts with children (art. 187) in 2025 by nationality and residence status (Swiss 73.2%) and the 784 accused (Swiss 62.0%), annually and nationwide. Residence status is a proxy, not ethnicity, and victims and accused are not linked; no rates for this offence.

BFS publishes victimization rates per 1,000 for children aged 0-14 by nationality group for simple assault (Swiss 1.09, EU/EFTA 1.24, other Europe 1.25, other 1.49; 2020-2024, domestic violence excluded) and accused of violent offences by residence status, all victims.

Neglect of the duty of care (art. 219) is in the police statistics database by accused residence status, but the table could not be retrieved (server error) and no child victims by origin are published; child-protection statistics have no origin variable.

Police statistics give 2025 homicide victims (8 under 18) and accused by residence status, all ages; the BFS homicide survey 2019-2023 gives victims and suspects of family homicides (46 children under 15) by nationality with rates per 100,000, not split by the child's age.

Police statistics give the 238 trafficking victims in 2025 (1 minor; Swiss 11) and 89 accused (Swiss 22) by residence status, and the victim-support statistics give counselled trafficking victims by nationality and age. All ages and forms.

Accused of pornography offences (art. 197, which includes child sexual abuse material but is not split) by residence status (2,332 in 2025; Swiss 1,535); victims of unauthorised sharing of sexual content (art. 197a, mostly not children) by residence status.

components.name: Victim heritage
components.full: Official data by harm that separately identify ethnic European children (e.g. White non-Hispanic, White British) alongside every other group, self-reported or official, few unknowns. Broad categories that lump ethnic Europeans with others get partial credit; proxies (nationality, citizenship, migration background, country of birth) at most 9.4 points.

components.name: Perpetrator heritage
components.full: Same standard for perpetrators: not perceived, few unknowns, ethnic Europeans separately identified. Proxies at most 9.4 points.

components.name: Coverage and missing data
components.full: Over 90% of the population covered, under 10% unknown

components.name: Rates and linkage
components.full: Rates per 100,000 possible, and victim heritage linked to perpetrator heritage

score.gold_standard: 100% means a country publishes data that separately identifies ethnic Europeans, both as perpetrators (so one can tell when they disproportionately harm a group) and as child victims (so one can tell when ethnic European children are disproportionately harmed), alongside every other group, linked victim to perpetrator, for every harm.
score.rules: Heritage is 75 of every 100 points (victims 37.5, perpetrators 37.5); coverage, rates and access share the other 25. Proxies such as nationality or migration background earn at most a quarter of the heritage points. A country with no real ethnicity data for victims or perpetrators is capped at 25%.
score.why: Switzerland scores 25% on the stricter scale (20-40%). The Federal Statistical Office publishes child victims and accused of sexual acts with children by nationality and residence status every year, child assault victimization rates by nationality group, and homicide and trafficking figures by residence status. All of this is nationality, a proxy, so the no-ethnicity cap rule applies.
score.weights_id: harm weights of 19 Nov 2026 (homicide 25, sexual abuse 20, sex trafficking 20, physical abuse 15, online exploitation 10, neglect 10)
